_README: Anchors for the v2 event-to-state stimulus set.
PROVENANCE. The author wrote 50 events across 10 attributes (see
anchors_template_filled.json). An LLM then drafted 27 more, plus the two
reply-style attributes replytone and replyformat, to close structural gaps
-- every attribute needs >=3 states and >=2 events from the same state for
the T3/T4 conditions to be constructible.
All 77 causal claims have since been read and endorsed by the author, so
`source` is 'author' for every event: it records validation status, not
authorship. `origin` keeps who drafted it first ('author' or
'llm_drafted') so the distinction stays recoverable, but results are NOT
split on it -- the endorsement is what the ground truth rests on.
`force` marks which way each event pushes, and it decides whether the T4
condition is sound for that anchor:
pull  the event makes the TARGET necessary or attractive on its own terms.
Its premise does not depend on what the user currently does, so it
still licenses the target when T4 swaps the setup value. T4 VALID.
push  the event REMOVES the original from-state. Its premise is about that
state, so once T4 swaps the setup value the premise no longer
concerns the stated preference and the keyed answer is not
derivable. T4 for these items instead tests whether the model keeps
a preference the event does not bear on -- where keeping it is the
CORRECT behaviour, i.e. the scoring is inverted.
A push event whose premise happens to cover the swapped-in state as well is
marked pull, because the item still works (renovation, relocation, heat).
Drafted by review of all 77 `effect` fields; see event_force_review.txt.
Renamed to avoid collisions: cooking->mealprep (states homecook/takeaway/
batch), learning state reading->books, shopping event mobility->walking.
family: 'life' = what the user does; 'style' = how the assistant replies.
